images.title: Total to daily bar
images.purpose: Recap the method: take a monthly total, divide by the days in that month, then draw that value as a bar on the scale.
images.composition: A left to right flow of three steps across the middle: a total card, a divide arrow, and one bar on a small scale at the right; plenty of white space between steps.
exact_structure: Left: one rounded card with a teal (#0072B2) outline reading 465 hours in August.
Middle: one thick grey (#6B7280) arrow pointing right with the label ÷ 31 days above it.
Right: a short vertical axis with 5 guidelines numbered 0, 5, 10, 15 and 20, and exactly 1 amber (#E69F00) bar reaching exactly the 15 guideline.
Above the bar, the label 15 hours a day in reddish purple (#CC79A7).
No other bars, months or numbers.
rejection: the bar not ending exactly at the 15 guideline
images.takeaway: Each daily bar comes from dividing the month's total by its number of days.
images.description: A card reading 465 hours in August, an arrow labelled divide by 31 days, and one bar reaching 15 hours a day.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Ask how the divisor would change for June or February before students draw their own bars.

image_decisions.why: A three step flow recaps the method the practice tool asks students to repeat.
